entities.summary: Sextius Niger was a Roman writer on pharmacology during the reign of Augustus or a little later. His works, particularly on the subject of medicinal plants, were influential in the development of Western pharmacology. The exact nature of his contributions is unclear, as many of his writings have been lost to time, but his legacy can be seen in the works of later Roman physicians. The Roman Empire's emphasis on scientific inquiry and the exchange of knowledge with other cultures during this period laid the groundwork for the advancements of later centuries.
